newsitem.title: FRANCE: French capital markets closing report.
newsitem.headline: French capital markets closing report.

text.p: French bond futures settled little changed after a lacklustre session with most looking to the implications of Friday's U.S. non-farm payrolls report for U.S. long-bond yields and the likely impact on European yields.
The March contract survived early jitters, finding support at 127.76/80, and then traded within a narrow range to settle down 0.04 at 126.86.

Volume picked up slightly, some 64,000 contracts changed hands, but traders said there was still a certain amount of caution among those recently returned after Christmas break, especially with the key jobs report looming.
"Clearly the European markets no longer have much buoyancy and we can assume most people have returned," Damien Jamet, analyst at FIMAT, said. "It's the usual worries."
Jamet said he expected the March bond contract to remain between 127.48/54 and 128.30/40 until the publication of the U.S. jobs report.
Economists polled by Reuters expected some 192,000 new jobs to have been created in December.
Another trader said while there were reasons to be confident about the short end of the curve people were cautious about the long end.
PIBOR contracts, still well supported by hopes for further interest rate cuts in France, received an additional boost from the relative strength of the franc.

Hit on Friday by expectations of faster interest rate cuts in France following the appointment of two allies of President Jacques Chirac to the Bank of France monetary policy council, the franc got support from a more buoyant dollar.
Languishing at 3.3812 per mark early on Monday, the French unit climbed as high 3.3763 and was trading at 3.3775 late in the session.
The 10-year yield spread between French and German benchmark bonds remained stable on Monday at minus six, compared with minus seven on Friday.

As expected the Bank of France left interest rates unchanged at its regular money market tender on Monday. The first meeting of the new monetary policy council, when changes in rates are usually agreed, was scheduled for January 16.
Call money was unchanged at 3-3/16 5/16 percent.
